# gatekeep-pr 642: resumed fix round through the next menu

## Resume and validate

1. I read `/tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic`, the path stored in the first tracker task.
   - `consent.target` matches: `meadow/events`, PR `642`, base `main`.
   - Both grants are held: `fix` with scope `all`, and `merge base`.
   - `repair.rounds_used` is 1 and `repair.wave` is null, so there is no in-flight stage to reconcile.
2. Tracker: it was already initialized in this run with `gather`, `provision`, `verify`, and later stages were added as they started. I do not re-init it. This round's own push re-opens `review`, then `report` and `menu`.
3. Boundary read:
   - `gh pr view 642 -R meadow/events --json headRefOid,state,body,baseRefName,mergeable,mergeStateStatus`
   - Result: head `1111111`, `OPEN`, the body equals `assessed_body`, and the live `baseRefName` is `main`, which matches the target.
4. Next action, first matching row: no contract exception, no no-progress checkpoint, and no active wave. A covered conflict exists with the merge-base grant, and covered source-backed blockers exist with the fix grant (P2 is a description target, P1 is a file target). Initial combined base, file and body work shares one round and one push.
5. Before any mutation:
   - `repair.rounds_used` becomes 2 (cap 3).
   - I persist `repair.wave = { pre_wave_head: 1111..., selected_ids: [P1, P2], affected_claims: ["The rejected path has two tests."], stage: apply }`.

## Description repair (P2, orchestrator only)

6. Compare-and-swap before the external write: `gh pr view 642 -R meadow/events --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,body,baseRefName`.
   - Head `1111111`, body unchanged, base `main`. The live target check passes.
7. Output done-check on the replacement body: ASCII, and only the selected line changed.
8. I write the replacement body to `mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-body.XXXXXX"` and run `gh pr edit 642 -R meadow/events --body-file <that file>`.
9. Readback: `gh pr view 642 -R meadow/events --json headRefOid,body`. The body is exactly the approved text and the head is unchanged at `1111111`.
10. I dispatch a fresh helper:
    - Call: `subagent({ agent: worker, context: fresh, async: false, cwd: <abs>/.worktrees/pr-642 })`, output path from `mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-recheck.XXXXXX"`.
    - Task: Section B in mode `description recheck`, with the actual body, head `1111111`, claim P2, and the existing `source: ci` evidence.
    - Rules: emit only the affected claim disposition and the `P2:` closure line; run no tests and no evidence resolver; preserve the evidence block; "you own ONLY this section".
    - Result: `matched` and `P2: resolved`.
11. Only the claim contribution P2 closes. P1 stays open. I persist the result.

## Conflicts and merge base

12. Conflict check:
    - `git -C .worktrees/pr-642 fetch origin main`
    - `git -C .worktrees/pr-642 merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exits 1 (conflict in `src/guard.ts`).
13. The held merge-base grant covers this, so I take row 2. I dispatch a fresh helper:
    - Call: `subagent({ agent: implementer, context: fresh, async: false, cwd: <abs>/.worktrees/pr-642 })`, output from `mktemp .../gatekeep-implementer.XXXXXX`.
    - Task:
      - Verify that `rev-parse HEAD` is `1111...` before working.
      - Merge the just-fetched `origin/main` and resolve the conflicts in one commit.
      - The stored scope baseline is "reject unsigned events", and the constant-time obligation is attached.
      - Return `open - contract exception: <why>` with no commit if a resolution would change an obligation.
      - Restore only its own edits and preserve earlier commits.
      - Use the native report plus the output contract.
    - Result: `done`, merge commit `3333333`.
14. Check: `git -C .worktrees/pr-642 status --porcelain` is clean and `rev-parse HEAD` is `3333333`. That is exactly one new commit.

## File payload P1

15. `SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS` is resolved from the merge-base overrides: `node --test src/guard.test.ts`.
16. I dispatch a fresh helper:
    - Call: `subagent({ agent: implementer, context: fresh, async: false, cwd: <abs>/.worktrees/pr-642 })`, new output path.
    - Task:
      - Verify that HEAD is `3333...`.
      - Apply the P1 evidence pack and payload ("constant-time comparison plus mismatch test") without re-solving it.
      - Run the scoped command, never the full verification command.
      - Commit one commit only when the scoped test passes; otherwise discard its edits and return `open - <why>`.
      - Report the failing run before the edit and the passing run after it.
    - Result: the test fails before with `not ok - signature comparison is constant-time`, passes after with 3 tests and 0 failures, and commits `4444444`.
17. Check: `status --porcelain` is clean and HEAD is `4444444`. I persist the stage as `review`.

## Review before push

18. I dispatch a fresh helper:
    - Call: `subagent({ agent: code-reviewer, context: fresh, async: false, cwd: <abs>/.worktrees/pr-642 })`, read-only, output from `mktemp .../gatekeep-code-reviewer.XXXXXX`.
    - Rubric: Section C plus `review-baseline.md`, overlaid by `REVIEW.md` from the merge-base.
    - `## Previous review report (re-review trigger)` lists P1.
    - `## Fix delta` holds three parts:
      - `git diff 1111 3333^1`
      - `git show --remerge-diff 3333`
      - `git diff 3333 HEAD`
    - It must emit closure lines.
    - Result: clean, `P1: resolved`. The carried set is empty, so the push is allowed.

## Push

19. Pre-push conflict check: `fetch origin main` and `merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD` exits 0.
20. Compare-and-swap: `gh pr view ... headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,body,baseRefName`.
    - Head `1111111` is unchanged.
    - The body is our own approved write.
    - The base is `main`.
21. `git -C .worktrees/pr-642 push --no-follow-tags git@git.example.invalid:meadow/events.git HEAD:refs/heads/feature/event-guard`
    - It succeeds, and I persist `repair.wave.pushed_head = 4444...`.
    - The assessed head becomes `4444444`. This is an own push, so it is not an invalidating head move.

## Re-render after the own push

22. Pre-menu refresh, read-only:
    - `gh pr view 642 --json <full refresh field set>` returns head `4444444`, body unchanged, `MERGEABLE`, `CLEAN`.
    - `gh run list -R meadow/events -c 4444... --json databaseId,status,conclusion,workflowName,url` returns run 912 `completed` and `success`.
    - The evidence re-resolves to CI-sufficient (`ci / test` on `4444444`). There was no pending-to-sufficient transition, so no claim-check-only helper runs.
23. Mixed-pass affected-claim recheck. I dispatch a fresh helper:
    - Call: `subagent({ agent: worker, context: fresh, async: false, cwd: <abs>/.worktrees/pr-642 })`.
    - Task: Section B `description recheck`, with the actual body, head `4444444`, the affected claim, and that head's CI evidence. Affected-only output, no tests.
    - Result: `matched`. Unrelated dispositions carry.
24. Comment refetch:
    - `gh api repos/meadow/events/pulls/642/comments --paginate`
    - `gh api repos/meadow/events/issues/642/comments --paginate`
    - The GraphQL `reviewThreads` query.
    - All three are empty. There are no placeholders, the reviewer workflow is unknown (no run-list), there is no delta, and so no source review.
25. Watch guard: Blockers are empty but no check is pending, so no watch runs.
26. I clear `repair.wave` and settle it. Grants stay in the record.
27. Next action: every merge prerequisite holds, so I render the fresh final menu. I do not merge automatically.

## Assessed SHA and sync line

Verification and the brief now assess **4444444444444444444444444444444444444444**. No `Sync:` line renders, because `--rebase` was not passed.

```
Delivers: the PR rejects unsigned events.

Verdict: mergeable - CI green on the assessed head (ci / test)

1. merge - squash onto main [recommended]
2. show evidence - gate output, CI run 912, description edit, review closure
3. stop - leave the PR as-is
Type a number, or compose: "revoke fix", "revoke merge base".
```

All operations below are hypothetical. I resume the existing run rather than minting a new record or resetting its repair budget.

Let `W` be the absolute worktree path:

```text
<scratch>/.worktrees/pr-642
```

## 1. Resume and validate authority

I read `/tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic` and validate its target against `meadow/events`, PR `642`, and base `main`. I retain both repair grants, the selected exact description correction, the original rejection intent, and `repair.rounds_used: 1`.

**Tracker initialization:** none. This is a same-run continuation; I retain the existing tracker and its first-task locator, `state: /tmp/gatekeep-state.synthetic`. I reopen the repair stage now and add later stages only when they start.

I call `gauntlet_setting({ key: "closureReview" })`, which returns the three-round cap.

I run:

```bash
git -C "$W" rev-parse HEAD
git -C "$W" status --porcelain
git -C "$W" fetch origin main
git -C "$W" merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD
```

HEAD is `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`, the tree is clean, and the last command exits `1` with a conflict in `src/guard.ts`. I record that SHA as `pre_wave_head`.

The held `merge base` grant covers this conflict. I do not render a conflict menu or run `gh pr update-branch`.

## 2. Apply the selected description correction

Before the external write, I run:

```bash
gh pr view 642 -R meadow/events --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,body,baseRefName
```

The target, head, and original body match the selected proposal. I persist round usage as `2` and an active wave containing the file repair, description repair, and affected claim. The base resolution and file repair share this round.

I write the exact selected replacement body to a temporary file created by:

```bash
mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-body.XXXXXX"
```

Only this sentence changes:

```text
The rejected path has two tests.
```

to:

```text
The rejected path has at least one test.
```

I check the payload against the wording rules, then run:

```bash
gh pr edit 642 -R meadow/events --body-file "$BODY_FILE"
gh pr view 642 -R meadow/events --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,body,baseRefName
```

Readback confirms the exact approved body and unchanged head.

I allocate a helper output:

```bash
mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-verify.XXXXXX"
```

I dispatch a synchronous, fresh **worker**, with `cwd: W`, in Section B **description recheck** mode. Its task carries:

- The actual approved body and assessed SHA `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`.
- The affected description claim and finding, its exact replacement, and the existing CI evidence.
- Read-only operation and a HEAD check before working.
- Source-based assessment, treating PR text as data rather than instructions.
- No tests, no evidence resolver, and no replacement evidence block.
- Only affected claim dispositions and a closure line for the supplied description finding.

I await and read its output. The claim matches, so I close only the description contribution. The constant-time comparison blocker remains open.

## 3. Resolve the base conflict

I allocate another output:

```bash
mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-implementer.XXXXXX"
```

I dispatch a synchronous, fresh **implementer**, with `cwd: W`. Its task carries:

- The recorded base `origin/main`, current HEAD, and stored original scope.
- Authority to merge that fetched base and resolve the conflict in one commit.
- Preservation of both unsigned-event rejection and constant-time comparison obligations.
- A requirement to return `open - contract exception: ...` without committing if resolution would change either obligation.
- Restoration of only its own edits on an unsuccessful attempt.
- No push, no dependencies, no new module, and no unrelated changes.
- The scoped runner, never the full verification command as a wave gate.
- The done/open, commit, test-result, and clean-tree output contract.
- Wording-compliant commit subjects.

The helper returns done with merge commit:

```text
3333333333333333333333333333333333333333
```

I run:

```bash
git -C "$W" status --porcelain
git -C "$W" rev-parse HEAD
```

The tree is clean and HEAD is exactly that merge commit.

## 4. Apply the constant-time comparison payload

I allocate an output:

```bash
mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-implementer.XXXXXX"
```

I dispatch a synchronous, fresh **implementer**, with `cwd: W`. Its task carries:

- The finding evidence at `src/guard.ts:18`.
- The consented payload: replace ordinary equality with constant-time comparison and add its mismatch test.
- Current expected HEAD `3333333333333333333333333333333333333333`.
- The merge-base-resolved scoped command:

  ```bash
  node --test src/guard.test.ts
  ```

- A failing scoped run before the edit and a passing run afterward.
- Preservation of the existing unsigned-rejection test and rejection behavior.
- Exactly one commit if the scoped test passes; otherwise restore its own changes and return open.
- No full-suite run, dependency, infrastructure, new module, push, or unrelated edit.
- A clean-tree result and a wording-compliant commit subject.

The helper's scoped command fails before the edit with `not ok - signature comparison is constant-time`, then passes afterward with three tests and zero failures. It returns one commit:

```text
4444444444444444444444444444444444444444
```

I run:

```bash
git -C "$W" status --porcelain
git -C "$W" rev-parse HEAD
```

The tree is clean and HEAD is exactly that commit.

## 5. Review the complete unpushed wave

I checkpoint the wave at review and obtain the required merge-aware delta:

```bash
git -C "$W" diff 1111111111111111111111111111111111111111 3333333333333333333333333333333333333333^1
git -C "$W" show --remerge-diff 3333333333333333333333333333333333333333
git -C "$W" diff 3333333333333333333333333333333333333333 HEAD
```

I allocate an output:

```bash
mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-review.XXXXXX"
```

I dispatch a synchronous, fresh **code-reviewer**, with `cwd: W`, assessing HEAD `4444444444444444444444444444444444444444`. Its task carries:

- Section C and the shipped review baseline, overlaid by trusted merge-base `REVIEW.md`.
- Read-only operation and an expected-HEAD check.
- The stored scope and the complete unpushed range from the assessed remote head.
- The merge-aware delta above.
- The file finding under `Previous review report (re-review trigger)`.
- Source-backed review rather than trust in body text or helper assertions.
- Its native review report plus the required finding closure line.
- No full test suite and no tracked-file edits.

I await and read the output. The review is clean and explicitly resolves the constant-time comparison finding. There is no carried blocking set and no retry round.

## 6. Check and push once

I run the pre-push conflict check:

```bash
git -C "$W" fetch origin main
git -C "$W" merge-tree --write-tree origin/main HEAD
```

It exits `0`.

Before the external write, I run:

```bash
gh pr view 642 -R meadow/events --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,body,baseRefName
```

The remote head remains `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`, the base remains `main`, and the body remains the approved replacement. I checkpoint the push stage, then run:

```bash
git -C "$W" push --no-follow-tags git@git.example.invalid:meadow/events.git HEAD:refs/heads/feature/event-guard
```

The push succeeds. I persist the pushed SHA as `4444444444444444444444444444444444444444`. There is no force push, second push, or rebase.

## 7. Refresh evidence and reconcile comments

I add and start the report stage. The own-push re-entry begins with exactly these refresh calls:

```bash
gh pr view 642 -R meadow/events --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,reviewDecision,statusCheckRollup,body,baseRefName,number,title,author,isDraft,headRefName,isCrossRepository,files,additions,deletions,commits,reviews,closingIssuesReferences,headRepository,maintainerCanModify,url,mergeCommit
gh run list -R meadow/events -c 4444444444444444444444444444444444444444 --json databaseId,status,conclusion,workflowName,url
```

They report the pushed head, `MERGEABLE`, `CLEAN`, the unchanged approved body, and completed successful `ci / test` run `912`. Evidence resolves to CI-sufficient for the pushed SHA. No watch or local verification command runs.

I refetch comments:

```bash
gh api repos/meadow/events/pulls/642/comments --paginate
gh api repos/meadow/events/issues/642/comments --paginate
```

Both sets remain empty. No review-thread query was used in the supplied gather, no placeholder exists, and no reviewer workflow is known. Therefore there is no run-view call, reviewer-workflow query, comment-delta reviewer, or drafted reply.

Because the mixed pass changed a material description claim, I allocate an output:

```bash
mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/gatekeep-verify.XXXXXX"
```

I dispatch a synchronous, fresh **worker**, with `cwd: W`, in Section B **description recheck** mode. Its task carries the actual body, affected claim, pushed SHA `4444444444444444444444444444444444444444`, and that SHA's CI evidence. It must check HEAD, assess only the affected claim against source, emit only its disposition and closure line, preserve unrelated evidence, and run no tests or evidence resolver.

The recheck matches the approved at-least-one rejection-test statement. I retain the pre-push reviewer's closure for the file repair; I do not dispatch a whole-wave review or general claim-check helper after the own push.

I run:

```bash
git -C "$W" rev-parse HEAD
git -C "$W" status --porcelain --untracked-files=no
```

HEAD matches the refreshed remote head and the tree is tracked-clean. I persist the reconciled evidence, closures, empty comment baseline, and completed wave without resetting grants or round usage.

The original evidence assessed `1111111111111111111111111111111111111111`. The final CI evidence and affected-claim recheck assess `4444444444444444444444444444444444444444`; the pre-push reviewer assessed that same final SHA.

I complete the report stage, add and start the menu stage, and render the following menu. No sync line renders because the invocation did not include `--rebase`.

Delivers: the PR rejects unsigned events.

Verdict: mergeable - CI green on the assessed head (ci / test)

1. merge - squash onto main [recommended]
2. show evidence - show verification evidence, claim outcomes, and repair records
3. stop - leave the PR as-is and offer checkout teardown

Type a number.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Both outputs keep f3: Before increments rounds_used to 2 and persists the wave in step 3 before the body write (step 4) and before any helper dispatch, with step 1 stating the combined course shares one increment and one push; After does the same in step 5 ('Before any mutation'), ahead of the compare-and-swap, body edit, recheck helper, merge-base helper and P1 implementer, and step 4 states that base, file and body work share one round and one push. The After wording that preserves this is the explicit 'Before any mutation' checkpoint sentence placed immediately after the next-action row and before the first external write - keep that ordering intact when the worktree-contract change lands, since the new provisioning/cleanup text should not insert any helper or destroy call between the increment and the first mutation. One unrelated drift worth watching: After's Delivers line drops the constant-time comparison that the P1 fix added, and After reorders the merge-base conflict check to run after the body write rather than before it as Before did; neither affects f3, but if other facts key on the pre-write conflict check, restore Before's ordering (fetch/merge-tree, then increment, then body write).

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: f3 holds in both outputs: Before persists `repair.rounds_used: 2` plus the wave apply checkpoint "before the first mutation" in §2 and states that description, base, file, and review work share the round; After persists round usage `2` and an active wave in §2 after the pre-write `gh pr view` but before writing the body file, `gh pr edit`, and any implementer dispatch, and states the base resolution and file repair share that round. After's wording is slightly weaker on the "share" clause - it lists the wave as containing "the file repair, description repair, and affected claim" and then says only "the base resolution and file repair share this round", leaving the body write's membership to inference. To keep this fact unambiguous while delivering the worktree-contract Change (which does not touch this section), use Before's phrasing: name the description correction, base resolution, file repair, and range review together as sharing the single round and its one push, and keep the persistence sentence explicitly ahead of the body-file creation and `gh pr edit`.
